Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Let <MATH_0002> be a big <ACCENT_0001>tale
site containing <MATH_0003>.
The structures <MATH_0004>, <MATH_0005>, and <MATH_0006>
are sites.

Let us show that <MATH_0001> is a site. It is a category with a
given set of families of morphisms with fixed target. Thus we
have to show properties (1), (2) and (3) of
Sites, Definition <REF_0001>.
Since <MATH_0002> is a site, it suffices to prove
that given any covering <MATH_0003> of <MATH_0004>
with <MATH_0005> we also have
<MATH_0006>.
This follows from the definitions as the composition of <ACCENT_0001>tale morphisms
is an <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Let us show that <MATH_0007> is a site.
Reasoning as above, it suffices to show that the collection
of standard <ACCENT_0003>tale coverings of affines satisfies properties
(1), (2) and (3) of
Sites, Definition <REF_0002>.
This is clear since for example, given a standard <ACCENT_0004>tale
covering <MATH_0008> and for each
<MATH_0009> we have a standard <ACCENT_0005>tale covering <MATH_0010>, then
<MATH_0011> is a standard <ACCENT_0006>tale covering
because <MATH_0012> is finite and each <MATH_0013> is affine.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
We omit the proof that <MATH_0014> is a site.
